question.problem:
Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x).$

$\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,\frac{625{x}^{4}}{4}+⋯$
question.worked_solution:
The Maclaurin series for $\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-5x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-5x) & =(-5x)-\frac{1}{2}(-5x)^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(-5x)^{3}-\frac{1}{4}(-5x)^{4}+⋯ \\  & =-5x-\frac{25{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{125{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{625{x}^{4}}{4}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
